title: Multitask linear contextual bandits with a shared low-rank representation
summary: Multiple linear bandit tasks share an unknown low-dimensional representation. All task actions must be submitted together before the batch of scalar rewards is revealed. Performance is the sum of cumulative pseudo-regret across tasks. Each task’s predictable action set may change over time.

model.instance: There are $M$ parallel tasks, each with $T$ rounds and one action per task per round. The parameter matrix and shared representation satisfy $$\Theta=[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_M],\qquad \operatorname{rank}(\Theta)\le r,\qquad \|\theta_m\|_2\le1.$$. Current action sets $\mathcal A_{t,m}\subseteq B_2^d(1)$ may depend on past history and are revealed before the full action batch. No task-diversity or covariance-eigenvalue lower bound is imposed.

operations.query_signature: Submit all $M$ actions simultaneously, then receive all rewards together. No action may use an earlier response from the same batch. $$Y_{t,m}=\langle x_{t,m},\theta_m\rangle+\eta_{t,m}.$$ Conditional on the past and chosen actions, noise has mean zero and is $1$-sub-Gaussian. Centralized causal learning is allowed. Inputs $M,d,r,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and current action sets are public; the shared representation $B$ and individual $w_m$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.
